items.text: WTI and Brent are down ~5% from the previous week (WTI 89.62 vs 94.05, Brent 92.14 vs 97.96), but energy prices remain elevated as an energy shock clouds the ECB's outlook with upside risks for inflation. For high-yield and stressed credit, elevated energy costs continue to pressure margins in energy-intensive sectors and consumer-focused names reliant on fuel hedges.

The ISM Services Prices Index stayed elevated at 73 in October, exceeding 70 for seven of eight months, with nineteen commodities reported up in price including fuel for a ninth straight month. Year-ahead inflation expectations decreased to 4.3% in preliminary November Michigan data from 4.7% in October. Core inflation remains sticky (core PCE 3.12% YoY as of September), creating asymmetric risk for lower-credit-quality borrowers unable to pass through costs.

ADP private payrolls added 86,000 jobs in October, mostly in services. Claims are drifting higher at 200k (up from 191k prior), and unemployment sits flat at 4.1%. While headline payrolls showed 165k in October (vs. 60k prior), the trend has cooled significantly. Watch for sustained deterioration in job creation—a sudden brake could trigger covenant stress across leveraged credit.

The Fed holds at 4.0% with the curve at 30bps (2-10y), slightly steeper than 25bps prior. The ECB deposit rate remains at 2.50% as of November 13, 2026. As of November 11, 2026, OIS pricing implies a 94% chance of a 25bp ECB hike at the December 17 meeting, with markets pricing 66.8bp of hikes over the next 12 months. Policy is slowly diverging (Fed pausing, ECB likely to hike), which could widen dollar-denominated credit spreads and stress cross-currency hedges.

High-yield OAS tightened slightly to 334bps from 330bps, while CCC spreads eased marginally to 1,310bps from 1,330bps. IG OAS held steady at 90bps. ISM Services PMI fell to 54.5 in October, below the 54.8 forecast. The slowdown in service activity signals potential stress emerging in credit-sensitive segments; monitor refinancing calendars closely for mid-market and CCC names with maturities clustering in 2027–2028.

U.S. retail sales rose just 0.2% month-on-month in October, down from September's 0.8% increase. The University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index rose to 51.0 in early November 2026, up from 48.0 in October. Housing remains under pressure with existing home sales at 3.75M (October), down from 3.97M (prior). The sentiment bounce is real but off historical lows; sustained weakness in durable orders and mortgage rates elevated at 7.11% constrain housing recovery, pressuring RMBS and CRE-linked credit.

GDPNow stands at 3.38% (preliminary Q4 tracking), up from 3.27%, and Q3 actual came in at 3.4%. Control-group retail sales rose 0.6% in October versus 0.3% expected, with consumer spending positioned to make a respectable though more modest contribution to Q4 GDP growth than Q3. Growth is decelerating but remains above trend; watch for revision lower if labor deteriorates or credit stress spreads to investment-grade names.

themeCards.title: China Manufacturing Contraction Risk
themeCards.statusLine: China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October from 50.1, below the 49.9 median forecast and below the 50 threshold that separates expansion from contraction. Production, new orders, and new export orders all fell below 50 in the same month.
themeCards.relevance: China growth deceleration feeds into emerging-market credit stress and reduces demand for US export-linked credits; multinationals with China exposure face margin compression. Watch for spillover into Asian and cross-border leveraged loans.

themeCards.title: Persistent Core Inflation & Pass-Through Ceiling
themeCards.statusLine: Services sector Prices Index stayed elevated at 73 in October, with nineteen commodities reported up in price including fuel for a ninth straight month. Long-run inflation expectations fell to 3.4% in November from 3.5% in October.
themeCards.relevance: Persistent input cost inflation meets consumer pushback (sentiment weak at 51 historically), leaving mid-market companies unable to fully pass through costs. BBB to CCC names with weak pricing power face EBITDA compression; refinancing risk rises if profitability erodes.

themeCards.title: Retail Momentum Stalling Into Year-End
themeCards.statusLine: U.S. retail sales rose just 0.2% month-on-month in October, down from September's 0.8% increase. Furniture and home furnishing sales fell 2.3%, while clothing and sporting goods each dropped 0.7%.
themeCards.relevance: Holiday season demand is a key refinancing and earnings driver for consumer-facing credit (retail, apparel, furniture, e-commerce). October's weakness signals consumer budget constraints and suggests risk of shortfall in Q4 results, pressuring covenant compliance and equity cushions in LBOs tied to seasonal peaks.

themeCards.title: ECB Rate Hike Path vs Fed Pause Divergence
themeCards.statusLine: OIS pricing implies 94% chance of ECB +25bp at Dec 17 meeting, with markets pricing 66.8bp of hikes over the next 12 months. The Fed remains paused at 4.0% with limited near-term cuts priced in.
themeCards.relevance: Diverging policy tightens dollar, widens cross-currency basis, and pressures euro-denominated and cross-border credit hedges. Refinancing risk rises for entities with FX mismatches or euro-denominated debt; watch for covenant stress in syndicated loans with USD/EUR basis triggers.

themeCards.title: Labor Market Deceleration Signal
themeCards.statusLine: Claims drifting higher at 200k (vs 191k prior), and payroll growth has slowed substantially. ADP private payrolls added 86,000 jobs in October, mostly in services. Unemployment remains flat at 4.1%, but employment momentum is visibly cooling.
themeCards.relevance: Sudden deterioration in job creation could trigger mass covenant stress across leveraged credit and middle-market loans with leverage or interest-coverage maintenance covenants. Watch for downgrades in Q4 earnings; default probability rises if unemployment accelerates above 4.5%.

themeCards.title: High-Yield Spread Complacency With Deteriorating Fundamentals
themeCards.statusLine: HY OAS at 334bps (essentially flat) despite slowing ISM Services (54.5), China PMI contraction, and retail weakness. CCC spreads at 1,310bps (easing from 1,330bps) even as distressed issuance risk rises.
themeCards.relevance: Spreads have not repriced downside scenarios (recession, credit event, rate shock). Special situations investors should position for volatility spike triggered by earnings misses, refinancing failures, or spread widening when yields stabilize or inflation surprises up. Relative value lies in CCC and distressed credit.

ecb.delta: Unchanged since Sept 16; +50bps YoY; market pricing 94% prob of +25bp hike Dec 17

chinaPMI.delta: Oct print below 50 for first time since July; weakness in production, orders, and exports; small/mid firms at 47.5-48.4

ismServices.delta: Oct actual 54.5 vs 54.8 forecast; new orders fell from 59.8 to 55.9; still expansionary but losing momentum

retailSales.delta: Oct actual 0.2% vs 0.1% consensus; down from Sept 0.8%; control group +0.6% vs +0.3% expected

existingHome.delta: Oct reading 3.75M SAAR vs prior 3.97M; mortgage rate 7.11% (Nov 12); inventory constraint ongoing

consensus.Retail Sales: October actual +0.2% m/m (released Nov 17), consensus was +0.1-0.2%
consensus.ISM Mfg: November data due Dec 1; October was 48.8
consensus.ISM Services: November data due Dec 3; October was 54.5 vs 54.8 forecast

regime.label: Late-cycle slowdown
regime.detail: Cooling labor & retail, sticky core inflation, elevated spreads, ECB hiking while Fed pauses, China contraction risk
